procedure.step: Register the factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (requires location outside a free zone, MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added; takes about 3 working days).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately. It may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.

Apply through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the service, fill in the application form, upload required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and submit the application.
Pay the certificate fee: AED 50 (band for invoice value up to AED 100000).
Receive approval, or a return with comments to correct; then print the approved certificate.
The certificate must be issued prior to, at, or within five working days of export, is valid for twelve months from issue, and covers one import.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020, and keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The tariff schedule prints 15%, but an exemption notification lowers the duty actually charged to 10%; the effective rate is used.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Mansha reads '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
